headline: Manchester City found guilty on 114 financial charges; faces potential title stripping, relegation
summary: An independent commission will now determine the penalties, which could range from points deductions and fines to player registration bans, or even relegation from the Premier League. The club is expected to appeal the verdict.
details: Manchester City has been found guilty on 114 of 115 financial charges by the Premier League. The BBC previously dubbed the initial hearing on these allegations as the "trial of the century" in sports.

While Manchester City has been found guilty, the specific sanctions are yet to be decided by an independent commission. The club is expected to appeal the verdict, which could prolong the final decision.

The 115 charges against City are categorized into five areas. These include failing to provide accurate financial information, details on player and coach remuneration, compliance with UEFA Financial Fair Play rules, adherence to Premier League Profit & Sustainability Rules, and a lack of cooperation with the Premier League's investigation.

Most of the charges span the 2009-10 to 2017-18 seasons. During this period, Manchester City secured eight major domestic trophies, including three Premier League titles, three League Cups, and two FA Cups.

Although the charges are proven, these titles are not automatically revoked. However, stripping past achievements, including trophies, is among the potential penalties. The commission's decision will clarify the specific events leading to any such judgment.

Other potential sanctions include points deductions, which could be applied in the current or future seasons, and substantial fines. Bans on player registration or transfers, and temporary suspensions from Premier League matches, are also possibilities.

The most severe punishment could be direct relegation from the Premier League to the Championship. This would mean losing their top-flight status, potentially through direct expulsion rather than just a points deduction.

Beyond City's own achievements, the verdict could impact other clubs from the affected seasons. Any club claiming damage to their league position, prize money, or European competition qualification could have their claims separately considered.

As of now, nothing is final. Following the determination of sanctions, Manchester City will have the opportunity to appeal. The timeline for a definitive resolution, including any potential title revocations or relegation, remains uncertain.

headline: PM Tarique Rahman holds 30 engagements including 11 bilateral meetings in New York UNGA visit
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman engaged in extensive diplomatic activities during his four-day visit to New York, focusing on national interests, trade, investment, and global cooperation.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman concluded a four-day visit to New York for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), participating in 30 official engagements. This included 11 bilateral meetings with various countries, as confirmed by Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin.

Discussions during these meetings prominently featured Bangladesh’s national interests, trade, investment, manpower exports, and energy security. Regional cooperation, the Rohingya crisis, health, climate change, and international peace were also key agenda points.

The Prime Minister’s schedule comprised eight UNGA-related engagements, four high-level events on the sidelines, and 11 bilateral meetings. He also held discussions with international organizations and prominent personalities.

PM Rahman attended a breakfast meeting with top Wall Street investors hosted by JPMorgan Chase, exploring investment opportunities in Bangladesh. He also met the president of the International Peace Institute, where Bangladesh's return to democratic rule was welcomed.

A meeting with UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk addressed human rights, the rule of law, and the establishment of democracy in Bangladesh. Bilateral talks were also held with the Crown Prince of Kuwait, the Saudi foreign minister, and the UAE deputy prime minister and foreign minister.

These bilateral meetings covered protecting Bangladeshi workers' interests, increasing manpower exports, energy security, cooperation in the mineral sector, and boosting investment. The PM emphasized strengthening longstanding ties with Middle Eastern countries.

Other significant meetings included those with World Bank President Ajay Banga, UN Secretary-General António Guterres, UN Special Envoy on Myanmar Julie Bishop, and UN High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih. He also met with the Gates Foundation.

Bangladesh organized two high-level events focusing on the Rohingya crisis and maternal, newborn health, and midwifery. PM Rahman also addressed high-level events concerning climate change, just transition, and sea-level rise.

Prime Minister’s wife Dr. Zubaida Rahman also participated in eight high-level engagements, delivering remarks at four. Her engagements included the UN General Assembly’s Platform of Women Leaders and a high-level event on maternal and child health.

Overall, the Prime Minister and his entourage represented Bangladesh at approximately 80 engagements during the visit, prioritizing national interests. Mahdi Amin highlighted that the PM, as head of a democratically elected government, effectively represented Bangladesh on the global stage.
